structured_output.summary: On-target 3136 ppm transit gives Rp 17.68 Earth radii, no secondary; signal is new.
reasons: The signal is new: `exofop_tois`, `exofop_ctois` and `published_signal` are empty, `ephemeris_match_likely_sources` and `ephemeris_match_contaminated_stars` are empty, and the verification record (2026-10-17 09:16) shows no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-16. Nothing argues for a drop on grounds of prior knowledge.

The transit is real and repeatable: `MES` 38.93774 in S98; `other_sector_results` S32 TESS-SPOC recovered at SNR 45.9 against expected 35.9; `joint_search_snr` 62.5 against `joint_search_highest_null_snr` 16.7 with `joint_search_detected` True and `period_pile_up_ratio` 0.2. The all-sector figure shows a flat-bottomed transit with sharp ingress and egress in both the S98 QLP (200 s) and S32 TESS-SPOC (600 s) panels; `fit_period_days` 6.2599677 +/- `fit_period_error_days` 0.00000394.

The dip is on the target: `pixel_verdict` on target, `pixel_verdicts_by_sector` S32 SNR 10.9 and S98 SNR 7.7 with best star TIC 264626874 in both, `joint_difference_image_snr` 13.4. In both difference images the out-of-transit-minus-in-transit peak sits on the target pixel with the free-fit cross on the target. The S98 difference image shows weak residual structure on the bright stars near pixels (14,15) and (10,5), but the target pixel is by far the strongest. This, with `nfpp_mean` 0 and `nearby_scenarios_excluded` True, answers the only caution, 'neighbour able to cause dip' (`gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip`: Gaia DR3 3237833152757788800 at 27" G 15.5 needs 24%; Gaia DR3 3237833187117523712 at 57" G 15.6 needs 27%), neither of which lies under the difference-image peak.

The transit shape fits a companion of the target star: `stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio` 0.966, `fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis` 1.11, `odd_even_difference_sigma` 1.30, `secondary_depth_ppm` -18 +/- `secondary_depth_error_ppm` 34 against `secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm` 157 (the phase-0.5 panel of the figure is flat), and `transit_grazing` False with `fit_impact_parameter` 0.745 +/- `fit_impact_parameter_error` 0.0326, so the radius is constrained rather than grazing-degenerate.

The radius is below the stellar threshold: `planet_radius_earth_radii` 17.68 +/- `planet_radius_error_earth_radii` 0.88 (about 1.6 Jupiter radii) from `fit_radius_ratio` 0.0560 on `stellar_radius_solar_radii` 2.89514, a host LAMOST classes A1V (`lamost_spectra`, SNR g 504, fibre on the target). An inflated giant planet on a 6.26 d orbit around a hot A star is plausible; a brown dwarf or late-M companion is not excluded by the photometry and the CTOI comment should say so.

The ellipsoidal caution that drove the 'held' decisions of 2026-10-16 in the record no longer stands: the current step 9 gives `ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm` 163 +/- `ellipsoidal_amplitude_error_ppm` 107 (1.5 sigma), `ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector` S98 155 +/- 328 and S32 163 +/- 114, `ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses` empty, and step 9 `cautions` empty. The earlier 3.6 sigma single-sector detection (163 +/- 45) was an underestimated error, so I agree with the 2026-10-17 07:54 decision rather than the two 'held' decisions.

Gaia and LAMOST show no sign of a bright stellar companion: `gaia_ruwe` 1.19, `gaia_non_single_star` 0, `gaia_eclipsing_binary` False, `vsx_binaries` and `vsx_variables` empty, `gaia_rv_variable` False with `gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses` 0.264 (weak because `gaia_vbroad_km_s` 185.197 gives `gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s` 11.1). The second LAMOST spectrum (A2V at 4.6 arcsec, RV -20 vs -14 km/s, 'no Gaia source in the fibre') is most simply the same rapidly rotating star in an offset fibre; a 6 km/s shift is not significant at that broadening.

TRICERATOPS supports a planet on the target: `most_likely_scenario` TP on TIC 264626874, `fpp_mean` 0.1692 +/- `fpp_standard_deviation` 0.13, `triceratops_verdict` likely planet, `nfpp_mean` 0. It is not statistically validated (earlier runs in the record gave 0.01475 and 0.07462, so the FPP is run-dependent), which is consistent with proposing a candidate rather than a confirmed planet.

The pipeline-level sector depth disagreement (`depth_ppm_by_sector` S98 2770 +/- 57 vs S32 3385 +/- 45, `sector_depth_consistency_p_value` 2.64e-17) is a QLP-versus-SPOC processing effect, not a property of the star: uniform cutout apertures agree across sectors (`cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture` 2694-3096 ppm, `cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value` 0.699). The search `depth_ppm` 1671.1 is a BLS box depth and likewise not a concern against `fit_depth_ppm` 3136. Note this at submission; it is not a red flag.

Why not 'held': `released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification` is empty, and the pending `unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star` 110 would not decide the open question. With per-sector ellipsoidal precision of about +/- 110 ppm, one more sector cannot separate a ~0.1 solar-mass companion (expected ~163 ppm, 1.5 sigma) from a planet; what decides the mass is radial-velocity or Doppler-tomography follow-up of this `tmag` 10.0672 A star, which a CTOI listing prompts. I therefore agree with the mechanical 'proposed for submission'.
